frontendExample.description: Code examples for common integrations, including issuing a Session token from the backend, streaming Chat responses with SSE, and handling token refresh.
frontendExample.overviewDesc: Choose the example that matches your integration flow.
frontendExample.overviewSessionDesc: The backend calls the Session API and returns client_token to the frontend.
frontendExample.overviewChatDesc: The frontend calls the Chat API and reads the SSE stream with status, delta, and error events.
frontendExample.overviewMessagesDesc: The frontend calls the Messages API with a Bearer token and retrieves the message list for a conversation.

feSession.title: Example: Session (backend)
feSession.description: Backend example that calls the Session API with a Server API Secret and returns client_token and expires_at to the frontend.
feSession.backendOnlyDesc: Call the Session API only from your server with a Server API Secret. Browser calls are not supported because CORS is disabled for /session.
feSession.exampleTitle: Issue a token from the backend
feSession.exampleDesc: Your server calls the Session API and returns the token to the frontend. The frontend then uses this token when calling the Chat API.

feChat.title: Example: Chat (SSE)
feChat.description: The Chat API does not return a single JSON body. It returns an SSE stream, so receiving and parsing the response is different from a normal API call.
feChat.streamingNoteDesc:
After POST /chat, the response body is a Server Sent Events stream.
Read the stream with a tool such as fetch and ReadableStream, then parse the event: and data: lines.
The event types are status for progress messages, delta for response fragments, and error for API failures with message and optional errorCode.
When an error event arrives, show the message in your UI and stop streaming.
feChat.callDesc:
Call POST /chat with Authorization: Bearer {'{'}token{'}'}.
The response is returned as a stream.
feChat.receiveDesc:
Read res.body with a reader, split the content by line, and parse the event: and data: pairs.
Append delta.text to build the full response, and use status.text for progress state.
When event: error arrives, call onStreamError and show data.message in the chat UI. The embedded chatbot widget shows it in the assistant status area.
If the HTTP response fails before the stream starts, show the JSON error message from the response body.

feMessages.title: Example: Messages
feMessages.description: Call the Messages API with the same Bearer token used for the Chat API. It returns the message list for the conversation, up to the latest 500 entries.
feMessages.callDesc: Call POST /messages with Authorization: Bearer {'{'}token{'}'}. You may omit plugin_key because the session token already identifies the tenant. If provided, it must match the token. conversation_id is also optional and defaults to the token's cid value.
feMessages.responseDesc: The response is JSON. data.messages contains an array of message objects with id, role, content, created_at, and locale, sorted by created_at in ascending order.

feIntegrated.title: Example: Integrated flow (with token refresh)
feIntegrated.description: Complete flow: the backend issues a token, the frontend calls the Chat API, and when FB_101 is returned, the frontend requests a new token and retries.
feIntegrated.frontendDesc: The frontend gets the token from your backend and calls the Chat API with it. When FB_101 is returned, request a new token, retry the request, and then read the SSE stream. See the Chat example for details.
feIntegrated.backendDesc: Your server calls the Session API with a Server API Secret and returns client_token and expires_at. Do not call the Session API directly from the browser.

quickStartSteps.1: Create a Server API Secret under Console > Development Settings > API Key Management. Then call POST /session from your backend with Authorization: Bearer <Server API Secret>. You may include user_id and project_id.
quickStartSteps.2: Pass client_token in the Authorization header as a Bearer token when calling POST /chat.
quickStartSteps.3: The Chat API streams responses with SSE. Include message in the request body. You may omit plugin_key because the session token already identifies the tenant.

session.title: Session API
session.description: The Session API issues a client_token that is valid for 5 minutes. Authenticate with a Server API Secret, then use the returned token as a Bearer token when calling the Chat API and Messages API.
session.backendOnlyDesc: Call this API only from your server with a Server API Secret. CORS is disabled for /session, so browsers cannot call it from another origin.
session.responseDesc: On success, data contains the following fields:

client_token.desc: Token string. Pass it as Authorization: Bearer {'{'}client_token{'}'} when calling /chat.

expires_in.desc: Token validity in seconds. The default is 300.

expires_at.desc: UTC Unix timestamp in seconds when the token expires.

conversation_id.desc: Deterministic ID derived from tenant_id, user_id, and project_id. It is used as the chat history document key. If both user_id and project_id are omitted, the value is an empty string.

plugin_key.desc: Tenant ID bound to the Server API Secret. Use this value as plugin_key for /chat and /messages, or omit plugin_key and use the tenant in the session token.

session.secretRequiredDesc: Pass Authorization: Bearer fb_sk_... with every /session request. Create and rotate secrets under Console > Development Settings > API Key Management. The full value is shown only once, when the secret is created.

errorsList.FB_302: The FREE plan cannot use this API

chat.title: Chat API
chat.description: Use a valid client_token from the Session API to call the streaming Chat API. Pass the token in the Authorization header.
chat.freePlanTip:
API endpoints are not available on the FREE plan.
Matching requests are blocked with 403 (FB_302).

plugin_key.desc: Plugin key (tenant ID). If provided, it must match the tenant in the session token. If omitted, the tenant from the token is used.

email.desc: User email address. When provided, it is stored with the chat and message data.

dataset_ids.desc: Array of dataset IDs for RAG search. When values are provided, only those datasets are searched. When omitted, the backend selects automatically.

chat.streamingDesc: Responses are streamed with Server Sent Events. Process each event as it arrives.

statusTypes.checking_sufficiency: Checking whether the available information is sufficient.
statusTypes.calling_model: Calling the model and preparing the response.

chat.responseDesc: The response is an SSE stream with the following event types:

delta.desc: Response fragment from the model. data: {'{'} "text": "..." {'}'}. Append fragments to build the full response.

error.desc:
API or stream error. data: {'{'} "message": "...", "errorCode": "FB_xxx" {'}'}, where errorCode is optional.
Show message in the chat UI and stop streaming.

errorsList.FB_302: The FREE plan cannot use this API
errorsList.FB_105: plugin_key does not match the session tenant

messages.title: Messages API
messages.description: The Messages API returns the messages for a conversation and uses the same Bearer token as the Chat API. When conversation_id is omitted, the cid value from the session token is used.

plugin_key.desc: Plugin key (tenant ID). If provided, it must match the tenant in the session token. If omitted, the tenant from the token is used.

conversation_id.desc: Conversation ID used as the chat document key. When omitted, the cid value from the session token is used.

messages.pluginKeyWhereToFind: You can find PLUGIN_KEY under Console > Development Settings > API Key Management.
messages.responseDesc: On success, data contains the following fields:

messages.desc: Array of message objects, sorted by created_at in ascending order. The API returns up to the latest 500 entries.

locale.desc: Locale for user messages. The value is null for assistant messages.

overview.intro:
is a chat widget that you can embed on your site.
With one script and one bootstrap block, a chat button appears in the bottom right corner. When clicked, it opens the chat panel.
overview.gettingStartedBefore: Add the snippet below to your page and set
overview.gettingStartedAfter: to the same pluginKey from the Console. data-plugin-key on the script tag is optional and is not read by the SDK.
overview.tip: Use the pluginKey issued from the Console.
overview.configFromConsoleNote:
When boot runs, the SDK loads Console channel settings, then applies client values from the boot payload.
Pass locale in boot for the initial language, and dataset_ids in update (or open) for the RAG scope.
The snippet only needs pluginKey; other values can be passed via boot and update.
overview.dataPluginKeyNote:
The SDK uses only boot({'{'} pluginKey {'}'}).
data-plugin-key on the script tag is optional and is not read by the SDK.
Keeping it in the snippet can make the key easier to see in DevTools, but it is not required for the widget to work.
overview.machineReadableSpecDesc: JSON document with commands, payloads, and integration notes. It can be used by crawlers, AI tools, and automation.

apiReference.callFormat: Call window.FrontierBase(command, payload). command is a string, and payload is an object that is passed only when the command needs additional data. After the script loads, window.FrontierBase.loaded is set to true.
apiReference.cmdBootRemarks:
pluginKey is required.
boot loads Console settings, then overrides them with client values from the payload such as locale, gaTrackingId, userEmail, and userPhotoURL.
Pass locale in boot to set the initial language for widget UI and the stream API (init and messages).
If you call boot again with the same pluginKey, the payload is applied like update.
apiReference.cmdUpdateRemarks:
Use update to change UI or runtime options after boot.
dataset_ids sets the default RAG scope for init (warmup) and message requests.
Calls made before boot are queued and applied after boot completes.
If update contains a different pluginKey, a new boot starts.
apiReference.cmdOpenRemarks:
Optional payload: dataset_ids.
If open is called before boot, the panel opens after boot completes.
apiReference.cmdDestroyPurpose: Remove the chatbot and clean up resources
apiReference.queueNoteIntro: Keep the queue stub in the snippet when chatbot.js has not loaded yet.
apiReference.queueNoteOutro: boot, update, and open calls made before the script loads are stored in the queue and run after the script is ready.
apiReference.pluginKeyDescription: Channel ID. It is used to fetch settings for the channel.
apiReference.modeDescription: Layout mode: 'floating', 'overlay-fullscreen', or 'push-sidebar'. Default value is 'floating'.
apiReference.bootPayloadLocaleBootDesc: Language code such as 'ko', 'en', or 'ja'. Overrides the Console locale. Used for widget UI and stream API responses (init and messages).
apiReference.localeDescription: Language code. Pass in update when the user changes language after boot. For the initial value, use locale in boot.
apiReference.bootPayloadUserPhotoUrlDesc: User profile photo URL. When provided, it is sent as userPhotoURL in stream requests.
apiReference.workspaceNameDescription:
Name shown in the panel header.
If no value is set, the SDK uses the default name for the current locale, such as 'Chat' in English or '채팅' in Korean.
apiReference.contentSelectorDescription:
CSS selector for the wrapper element that will be pushed in push-sidebar mode.
Set this when the main content is inside #app, #root, or a similar container.
When omitted, the SDK automatically detects common roots such as #app, #root, #__next, #__nuxt, #q-app, app-root, and main.
apiReference.gaTrackingIdDescription:
Google Analytics measurement ID in the G-XXXXXXXXXX format.
When passed to boot, it overrides ga_tracking_id from the Console.
This feature is available only on PRO and ENTERPRISE plans.
When enabled, the SDK loads gtag and calls gtag('config', id) once.
apiReference.openPayloadDatasetIdsDesc:
Array of dataset IDs for RAG search.
Pass in update to keep a default scope for init and message requests.
Pass in open to override only for that panel session.
When values are provided, they are sent as datasetIds in the request body. When omitted or empty, the backend selects automatically.
apiReference.updatePayloadNote:
update overrides Console and boot settings at runtime.
All fields below are optional.
You can call update before boot; values stay in the queue until boot completes.
Use locale when the language changes, and dataset_ids to set the RAG search scope.
apiReference.updatePayloadEmailDesc: User email address (userEmail). When provided, it is stored with chat and message data and sent with stream requests.
apiReference.updatePayloadColorCodeDesc: Color for the trigger and header as a hex value, for example #3e5bf0.
apiReference.updatePayloadButtonTextDesc: Label for the floating trigger. When set, the trigger appears as a pill button with text.
apiReference.updatePayloadWelcomeMessageDesc: Assistant welcome message shown when a new conversation starts.
apiReference.updatePayloadCoverImageDesc: Cover image URL for the conversation list header.
apiReference.updatePayloadDescriptionDesc: Channel description shown in the conversation list header.
apiReference.updatePayloadImgUrlDesc: Logo URL for the floating trigger when buttonText is not set.
apiReference.updatePayloadHideTriggerDesc: When true, the floating button is hidden. Open the panel from your own UI with open.
apiReference.updatePayloadDatasetIdsDesc:
Array of dataset IDs for RAG search.
Sent as datasetIds on init (warmup) and message stream requests.
Use update for a site-wide default scope, or open to change scope per panel session.
apiReference.datasetIdsBullet1: Array of dataset IDs used as RAG search targets.
apiReference.datasetIdsBullet2: When values are provided, they are sent as datasetIds in the request body, and only those datasets are searched.
apiReference.datasetIdsBullet3: When the value is omitted or an empty array, datasetIds is not sent and the backend selects appropriate datasets automatically with LLM based logic.
apiReference.datasetIdsBullet4: When you have two or more datasets, dataset_ids is recommended so the results are clearer.
apiReference.datasetIdsBullet5: For a site-wide default dataset scope, use dataset_ids in update. For per-page scope, pass dataset_ids on each open call.
apiReference.datasetIdInfoCard: You can find dataset_id under Console > Development Settings > API Key Management.
apiReference.debugNote:
Set window.__FRONTIERBASE__.debug = true to print logs in the console.
This option is intended for internal debugging and should be enabled only while troubleshooting.

gaTracking.intro: When gaTrackingId is passed to boot, or when ga_tracking_id is saved in the Console on a PRO or ENTERPRISE plan, the chatbot sends the following events to Google Analytics.
gaTracking.introBullet1: The SDK checks the G-XXXXXXXXXX format. It then loads gtag and calls gtag('config', id) once.
gaTracking.introBullet3: Event names are fixed, such as fb_chat_opened and fb_message_sent, and can be used directly in GA4 reports.
gaTracking.triggerMessageSent: Immediately after a message is sent
gaTracking.licenseNote: Available only on PRO and higher plans.

layoutModes.floating:
A floating button appears in the bottom right corner.
After a click, a rounded panel of about 380 x 600 px appears above the button. On mobile, the widget opens in full screen.
This mode is well suited for websites and landing pages.
layoutModes.overlayFullscreen:
The widget covers the entire screen and centers the mobile chat view.
Use this mode when the chat should take over the full view.
layoutModes.pushSidebarIntro: This layout pushes the main content, either body or the contentSelector wrapper, to the left and places the sidebar panel in the space that opens up.
layoutModes.pushSidebarBullet1: The sidebar does not cover the content.
layoutModes.pushSidebarBullet2: The content shifts to the side.
layoutModes.pushSidebarSpa: For single page applications, specify the main content wrapper with contentSelector instead of using the global body.
layoutModes.pushSidebarUseCaseBold: dedicated chat layouts on desktop where the content is pushed and the chat panel is fixed beside it
layoutModes.mobileNote: On mobile, floating and push-sidebar are ignored. The widget always runs in overlay-fullscreen mode.

codeExamples.example1Desc:

data-plugin-key is optional and used only for display.
codeExamples.example2Title: Example 2: locale in boot, dataset_ids in update
codeExamples.example2Desc: Pass locale and userEmail in boot, then set dataset_ids and UI options in update.
codeExamples.example3Desc: Initialize the widget with boot, then set mode: 'push-sidebar' and contentSelector with update.

codeExamples.example4Desc:
Remove only the boot line from the standard snippet.
Then only the SDK loads at first, and the floating button appears only after you call boot later in your code.
This is useful after login or after a button click.
Keep the queue stub in the snippet.
codeExamples.example4BootNote:
Call boot with locale when the chat button should appear, then set the RAG scope with dataset_ids in update.
If the SDK has not loaded yet, commands stay in the queue and run after loading.
codeExamples.example5Desc: After boot, you can change the mode or workspace name with update.

codeExamples.example6Desc: Open and close the chatbot panel from your own buttons.
codeExamples.example7Desc: Set a default RAG scope with dataset_ids in update, or scope a single panel session with dataset_ids in open.
codeExamples.example8Title: Example 8: Send GA events with gaTrackingId
codeExamples.example8Desc: Pass gaTrackingId to boot to send GA events. This feature is available on PRO and higher plans.

integrationGuide.scriptPositionDesc:
Place the script in the head or near the end of the body.
When using defer, keep the DOM order intact. A common placement is right before the closing body tag or in the header.
integrationGuide.spaHandlingDesc:
If a single page application clears and re-renders the body during route changes, the widget may be removed.
In that case, call window.FrontierBase('destroy') and then start again with window.FrontierBase('boot', {'{'} ... {'}'}) after navigation completes.
integrationGuide.wrapperTitle: When the main content is inside a wrapper
integrationGuide.wrapperDesc: In push-sidebar mode, set contentSelector to the main wrapper so the content is pushed correctly, for example #app or #root.
integrationGuide.allowDomainDesc:
In the Console under Install > Allowed domains, you can restrict which hostnames are allowed to run boot.
If the current hostname is not allowed, boot is blocked, a warning appears in the console, and the widget is not shown.
An empty list allows all domains.
frontierbase.io is always allowed.
integrationGuide.cspDesc:
Allow at least https://cdn.frontierbase.io in script-src.
If you use GA, also allow https://www.googletagmanager.com.
For connect-src, allow https://*.googleapis.com, https://*.firebaseio.com, and the Chat API at https://*.a.run.app.
For img-src, allow cover and logo URLs, plus data: if needed.
The widget UI uses Shadow DOM, not an iframe.

summary.pluginKeyIssueDesc: Find your pluginKey under Console > Development Settings > API Key Management, then pass it to boot({'{'} pluginKey {'}'}).
